SUST 1000.title: Sustainability Fundamentals
SUST 1000.description: This course provides students with an interdisciplinary perspective in comprehending the challenging issues on human sustainability on the limited planet earth. It also provides an overarching framework covering economic development, individual lifestyle and policies to deal with global, regional and local emerging issues to provide students with a good foundation for their sustainability related majors and minors.
cilos: Have a holistic appreciation of the issues relating to sustainability, including the role played by science, engineering, business, social science and the humanities in understanding these issues
Review and evaluate sustainability issues from multiple perspectives
Communicate balanced, evidence-based views of the issues and possible solutions
Contribute to sustainable futures with approaches and frameworks acquired through the course
Take a considered view of their own lifestyle choices and potential to contribute to sustainability as professionals and community leaders

SUST 1001.title: Special Topics in Sustainability
SUST 1001.description: This special topics course provides students with broad and useful knowledge of various emerging sustainability topics of introductory level with a goal to arouse students' interest in sustainability studies. May be repeated for credit, if the topics studied are different. Graded letter grade or P/F subject to different offerings.
cilos: Acquire an understanding of the useful knowledge of various emerging sustainability topics at introductory level.
(To be provided by the individual course when offered.)

SUST 1010.title: Introduction to Sustainability
SUST 1010.description: This course provides students with a holistic, interdisciplinary, evidence-based understanding of the challenge of ensuring the sustainability of humanity on a planet with limited natural and social capacities. The course introduces frameworks, approaches and key trade-offs underpinning efforts to deal with existing and emerging global issues and considers how these problems relate to our own lifestyles.
cilos: Assess issues (water, energy, economy, consumption, etc) relating to sustainability, including the role played by science, engineering, business, social science and the humanities in understanding these issues
Review and evaluate sustainability issues from multiple perspectives
Communicate balanced, evidence-based views of the issues and possible solutions
Apply the Technology and/or Lifestyle change approaches and the Business As Usual vs. Radical Change framework acquired through the course for sustainable future solutions
Review critically their own lifestyle choices and potential to contribute to sustainability as professionals and community leaders

SUST 1020.title: Climate Films and Sustainable Future
SUST 1020.description: This course bridges the artistic depiction of climate disasters in modern movies with the real science of climate change. By introducing and discussing seven films that depict extreme weather conditions, students will use these cinematic portrayals as starting points to delve into the physical science of the climate system. The course will cover the history of Earth’s climate, the ongoing challenges of climate change, and prospective technologies and strategies for a sustainable future. Students will gain fundamental knowledge of the climate system and its essential physical processes. Through immersive experiences, they will also learn to comprehend chronic environmental stresses and understand the pressures that drive sustainable behavior changes. Different pathways of sustainable development and their implications for policies and personal lifestyles will be discussed to inspire students to contribute to embrace and contribute to sustainability. Additionally, the course will explore the connections between art, science, and human behavior.
cilos: Give a brief history of the Earth’s climate
Describe the scientific processes leading to the extreme weather in the current climate
Explain the anthropogenic impact on climate change and its relations to human society development
Elaborate the concept of “tipping points” in climate change with examples and potential impacts on society
Explain major technologies and necessary human behavioral changes for mitigating global warming
Articulate different sustainable development solutions for mitigating the climate change impacts on our society

SUST 1030.title: Climate Change and Sustainability: An Interdisciplinary Perspective
SUST 1030.description: This undergraduate course provides an accessible and engaging introduction to the scientific and societal dimensions of climate change, with a focus on both global and local perspectives. Through an interdisciplinary approach, students will learn about the fundamental physical processes that drive climate change and contribute to extreme weather events such as heatwaves, droughts, wildfires, and floods. The course explores how these changes disrupt natural ecosystems, threaten biodiversity, influence economic stability, impact public health, and reshape international relations. It also examines a variety of strategies for adapting to and mitigating the effects of climate change, including policy responses, technological innovations, and community-based approaches, using real-world examples to connect scientific concepts to everyday life. Designed to foster critical thinking, this course equips students with the foundational knowledge and skills to understand and address climate change and sustainability challenges.
cilos: Explain the fundamental principles of climate change and sustainability
Apply climate change and sustainability concepts to real-world scenarios at local and global levels through interdisciplinary learning from academic and practical perspectives
Identify and propose evidence-based solutions to address climate change and sustainability challenges in community and professional contexts
Effectively communicate ideas and solutions related to environmental, social, and governance issues through collaborative projects and discussions

SUST 1101.title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Fundamentals
SUST 1101.description: This course examines the importance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors in managing modern corporations. Throughout the course, students will examine real-life examples to highlight why and to which extent ESG matters for firms and investors operating in various contexts.
cilos: Explain the fundamental concepts and importance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors in business
Analyze how environmental challenges, such as climate change and resource scarcity, impact business operations and strategic decision-making
Evaluate the social responsibilities of businesses, including labor practices, community relations, and human rights considerations
Critically assess key principles of corporate governance and their role in promoting ethical business practices and long-term sustainability
Apply ESG criteria to assess corporate performance and identify potential risks and opportunities
Compose strategies for integrating ESG considerations into business operations and decision-making processes
